examples.japanese: {蛇|へび}が{草|くさ}の{中|なか}にいた。
examples.english: There was a snake in the grass.

notes:
{蛇|へび} refers to snakes, legless reptiles.

KANJI READING:
Also read as じゃ in compounds (e.g., {大蛇|だいじゃ}, {蛇口|じゃぐち})

ZODIAC:
{巳|み} (snake) is the sixth animal of the Chinese zodiac. People born in the Year of the Snake are called {巳年|みどし}{生|う}まれ.

TYPES OF SNAKES:
- {毒蛇|どくへび}: venomous snake
- {青大将|あおだいしょう}: Japanese rat snake (common, non-venomous)
- マムシ: pit viper (venomous)

IDIOMS AND EXPRESSIONS:
- {蛇足|だそく}: superfluous addition (literally 'snake legs')
- {蛇|へび}の{道|みち}は{蛇|へび}: it takes one to know one
- {竜頭蛇尾|りゅうとうだび}: anticlimactic ending (dragon head, snake tail)

RELATED:
{蛇口|じゃぐち} (faucet/tap) contains the kanji for snake but refers to a water tap.
